metadata.title: 1999 Case 01
metadata.original_presentation: A 53-year-old right-handed man was admitted to the hospital in December because of fever and an altered mental state.

required.content: What was the patient's condition prior to admission?
required.response: The patient had been well until two weeks earlier, when a cough and rhinorrhea developed. Three days before admission, he became lethargic, febrile, and forgetful.

teaching_points.content: A sudden change in mental status and fever can indicate a serious underlying condition such as infection or neurological event.

required.content: What is the patient's medical history?
required.response: The patient had a history of impaired glucose tolerance but was said to have avoided medical care. He did not drink alcohol or take medications or illicit drugs, and he had no pets.

teaching_points.content: Impaired glucose tolerance can be a risk factor for various complications, including infections.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Bacterial Meningitis
refuting_evidence: absence of neck stiffness or photophobia noted

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Metabolic Encephalopathy
refuting_evidence: presence of fever and recent respiratory symptoms

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Autoimmune Encephalitis
refuting_evidence: presence of fever and recent respiratory symptoms

required.content: What were the findings on physical examination upon admission?
required.response: The patient was pharmacologically paralyzed, with an indwelling bladder catheter. He was markedly obese. On neurologic examination, he was unresponsive to voice or to noxious stimuli but intermittently gagged on the endotracheal tube. The pupils were equal and minimally reactive to light. There was no response to the doll's-head maneuver. The corneal reflexes were weak. The deep-tendon reflexes were ++ and equal; bilateral Babinski signs were present.

teaching_points.content: Neurological examination findings such as Babinski signs and weak corneal reflexes can indicate severe brain dysfunction.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Bacterial Meningitis
refuting_evidence: absence of neck stiffness noted in the case
additional_information_needed: CSF analysis for cell count, glucose, protein, and culture

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Non-convulsive Status Epilepticus
refuting_evidence: no specific mention of seizure activity or subtle motor signs
additional_information_needed: EEG to assess for seizure activity

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Diabetic Hyperosmolar Syndrome
refuting_evidence: no mention of hyperglycemia or dehydration symptoms

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Stroke
refuting_evidence: gradual onset of symptoms over days

required.content: What were the results of the initial CT scan?
required.response: A CT scan of the head showed diffuse white-matter hypodensity in both cerebral hemispheres, predominantly at and above the level of the basal ganglia. More discrete areas of hypodensity were seen in the right internal capsule and the left inferior frontal region, and there was mass effect, with obliteration of the perimesencephalic and peripontine cisterns.

teaching_points.content: CT findings of hypodensity and mass effect suggest significant cerebral edema and possible herniation.

required.response: The urine was positive for glucose (++++) and protein (++); the sediment contained 35 red cells, 4 white cells, and a few bacteria per high-power field. Serum tests for drugs of abuse were negative.

teaching_points.content: Presence of glucose and protein in urine can indicate renal involvement or systemic illness.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Viral Encephalitis
key_features: history of recent upper respiratory symptoms
supporting_evidence: CT findings of diffuse white-matter hypodensity
additional_information_needed: EEG to assess for encephalitis patterns

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis (ADEM)
refuting_evidence: age is less typical for ADEM
no clear post-vaccination or post-infectious trigger identified
additional_information_needed: MRI to better characterize white-matter changes

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Diabetic Hyperosmolar Syndrome with Cerebral Edema
refuting_evidence: no mention of hyperglycemia or serum osmolality
CT findings more suggestive of encephalitis

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Cerebral Vasculitis
refuting_evidence: no clear evidence of vessel involvement

required.content: What treatments were administered during hospitalization?
required.response: Ceftriaxone treatment was continued, and acyclovir, ampicillin, vancomycin, insulin, phenytoin sodium, mannitol, minidose heparin, and sucralfate were given. Repeated increases in intracranial pressure were managed with mannitol and pentobarbital.

teaching_points.content: Management of increased intracranial pressure often involves medications like mannitol and pentobarbital to reduce cerebral edema.
